intro_en: The Israel National Trail passes through Nahal Dishon, the largest of the streams of the eastern Upper Galilee, with a small spring, colourful spring blooms and flowing water in winter.
character_en: (For those walking north to south) The walk through Nahal Dishon is a gentle ascent along a dirt road. Most of the walk is exposed to the sun
transport_en: At the end point: Kibbutz Baram, close to the trail
pois_en: Ein Aviv, beautiful cliffs on either side of Nahal Dishon. Winter and spring blooms, small springs and flowing water in winter and spring
important_en: This is a relatively short segment. It can be extended by combining part of segment 6 (Baram - Mount Meron) and continuing to hike as far as the bend near the village of Tzivon or to Horvat Hamama.

Nahal Dishon used to be a very popular route for off-road vehicles, which made life difficult for hikers on foot. The Israel Nature and Parks Authority has physically closed the entrance to off-road vehicles, and the stream can now be hiked in peace.

After rains the stream may flow, and at times you will need to cross shallow water or hop across the stones above the water. On hot spring days it is sometimes possible to splash about in the pools or in the stream, but this is not clear, clean spring water.
description_en:
The walk along the Israel National Trail begins at the Alma Bridge, heading west on a dirt road that leads to the confluence of Nahal Aviv and Nahal Dishon. We walk about 5 km through open terrain exposed to the sun, with a few shady spots for resting and small pools depending on the season.
At the fork of Nahal Aviv and Nahal Dishon, we take the left-hand trail uphill. To the right, a blue-marked trail climbs into Nahal Aviv, which is slightly more challenging. After 2 km we reach Road 899 south of Kibbutz Baram, and cross it southwards towards the Baram Forest. In suitable weather there are several places to splash about in flowing water both north and south of the road. In winter and spring the stream often flows, most of the water coming from Nahal Gush Halav, which joins Nahal Dishon about a kilometre south of the road.
Option to extend the segment: since this is a relatively short segment, you can continue hiking along part of segment 6 (Baram - Mount Meron) as far as the bend near the village of Tzivon or to Horvat Hamama.
nearby_en: Nahal Aviv, "The Maidens" (HaAlamot) and the caves in the cliffs of the stream.
A tour and culinary options in the beautiful Circassian village of Rehaniya.
The observation tower at the Har Shifra campground in the Baram Forest, with a fine view over the whole area.
The Yiron Winery at Kibbutz Yiron.
lodging_en: Camping at the Har Meron Field School
author_en: Omer Shapira, content coordinator, Tourism Department, Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel (SPNI).
